through_line: This week's climbers competed on what to keep out of the context window, not what to pile in.
prior_through_lines: Issue 2 (2026-05-09): Agents are gaining persistent memory and self-composing skill loops between sessions.
Issue 4 (2026-05-26): This week's breakout repos pulled AI off the cloud and onto hardware the user owns.
Issue 5 (2026-05-31): This week's builds were connective tissue for agents, not new models.
Issue 6 (2026-06-07): The repos that climbed this week stayed thin and stood on tools that already worked.
evidence_paragraph: RLM (@a1zhang) places the prompt in a REPL variable and recurses over snippets, so RLM(GPT-5-mini) beats GPT-5 by 34 points at OOLONG 132k tokens for roughly the same cost, by never reading the whole document at once. LMCache (@ChengYihuaA) treats the KV cache as a shared layer pulled warm across engines instead of recomputed per request, claiming up to 15x throughput on multi-round and document workloads. ctx (@SteveSolun) walks a graph of 68,494 skills and loads only the 10-to-15 that matter, unloading the rest as rot. Three different layers, one move, decide what the model never has to hold.
counter_signal: Ollama (@ollama) and Superpowers (@obra) climbed on the opposite premise, raw local reach and an enforced process that adds structure rather than trimming it.
note: Distinct from prior four. Issue 2 was memory across sessions, Issue 5 was connective tissue, Issue 6 was thin tools on existing surfaces. This week is context economy, what to leave out of a single inference.
